newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes down after technical sell-off.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes down after technical sell-off.

text.p: IPE May Brent futures shed earlier gains on Wednesday, closing 20 cents lower at $17.73, as the contract was pushed down by last-hour technical selling after breaking through $18.00 support. "There's no new news out...It's pretty good trade selling on a break of $18.00," one broker said.
The May Brent contract gained value earlier in the day, hitting a high of $18.34 a barrel shortly after NYMEX opened.

Traders said the contract was buoyed earlier by technicals and the gains the contract made throughout most of the day followed modestly bullish weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory data, released late on Tuesday. "We went through support at $18.03 then (the psychologically important) $18.00 and then the stops got triggered," a second broker said of Brent's downward trend in the late trading in London.
Brokers said the next support level for May Brent was $17.65 -- the nine-month low it hit last Friday. Brent touched a low of $17.72 in late afternoon trade on.
April gas oil futures closed 25 cents down at $162.50 per tonne after good paper selling in the contract which expires on Thursday, brokers said.

"Obviously the market closed on the low side. We had a bounce an hour or so before the close back up to $163.50. Heating oil once again ticked off and we got a quite a lot of good paper selling in (April) gas oil," one broker said.
"Gas oil has actually given up a little bit against the heating oil," he added.
April gas oil closed $2.00 off the day's high of $164.50.
May gas oil, which hit a high of $166 in earlier trade, closed up 25 cents at $164.25.
